Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
17. Q: Why should attributes and relationships that apply only to a role be stored with that role?
A: Show answer
A party may be subject to different rules depending on its role. Credit rating and credit limit may apply when a party is a customer, while supplier qualification or payment terms may apply when it is a supplier. Storing these facts on PARTY would imply that they apply to every capacity in which the party participates. Storing them with the role keeps their scope explicit and prevents unrelated processes from interpreting them incorrectly. The same principle applies to role-specific contacts, responsibilities, statuses, and other relationships whose meaning depends on the capacity being modeled.
Study instruction: Select one party with customer, supplier, and employee roles. List three attributes for each role and identify any attribute that should remain at the shared PARTY level.
Key point: Place a fact at the level where its business meaning is valid.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
18. Q: Why does PARTY ROLE need its own identifier even when PARTY and role type are known?
A: Show answer
The chapter's model allows the same party to play the same role at different points in time. A distinct PARTY ROLE identifier can distinguish separate role instances, including a role that ends and later begins again or a role that has separate relationship contexts. It also gives relationship entities a stable object to reference instead of relying only on a party identifier and a role-type code. The implementation must define the uniqueness rules for role instances and prevent unintended duplicate active roles where the business requires only one.
Study instruction: Model one person who leaves employment and is rehired later. Decide whether the two periods should be represented as separate role instances and show how each is related to its employment record.
Key point: A role instance can have its own identity and lifecycle, distinct from the party and role type.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
19. Q: What kinds of person roles are illustrated in the model?
A: Show answer
The chapter identifies PERSON ROLE examples such as EMPLOYEE, CONTRACTOR, FAMILY MEMBER, and CONTACT. CONTACT represents a person acting as a representative for an organization or another party, such as a sales contact, support contact, customer contact, or supplier contact. These examples show that roles can represent employment, contractual engagement, family association, or representation. The list is illustrative rather than exhaustive. An enterprise should define role types that reflect its own responsibilities and business language while retaining the distinction between a person's identity and each role instance.
Study instruction: For each illustrated person role, state the business condition that makes it applicable, the party or organization it may relate to, and one attribute that belongs specifically to that role.
Key point: Person roles cover several distinct forms of participation, not just employment.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
20. Q: What organization roles are represented in the chapter, and what do they describe?
A: Show answer
Organization roles include DISTRIBUTION CHANNEL, COMPETITOR, PARTNER, REGULATORY AGENCY, HOUSEHOLD, ASSOCIATION, SUPPLIER, ORGANIZATION UNIT, and INTERNAL ORGANIZATION. They describe how an organization participates in the enterprise's environment. For example, a regulator oversees activities, a partner has an alliance, a supplier provides goods or services, and an internal organization is part of the enterprise being modeled. ORGANIZATION UNIT can further describe parent organizations, subsidiaries, departments, divisions, and other units. The list should be adapted to the enterprise's own structure and terminology.
Study instruction: Build a role catalogue for a sample enterprise. For each role, provide a definition, whether it applies only to organizations, and whether it normally requires a relationship to another party.
Key point: Organization roles express distinct business relationships and structural capacities.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
21. Q: What is the difference between an agent and a distributor as distribution channels?
A: Show answer
Both are organizations that market an enterprise's products, but they participate differently in the commercial flow. An agent markets products without buying or carrying the goods, while a distributor generally purchases the goods and then resells them. Treating both as an undifferentiated channel can obscure important differences in ownership, inventory exposure, contractual obligations, and operational responsibility. The role model therefore provides a way to classify the channel precisely while keeping the organization's identity separate from the role it performs for a particular enterprise or product context.
Study instruction: Compare an agent and a distributor in a simple order-to-delivery scenario. Identify who buys the goods, who carries inventory, and which facts belong to the organization versus its channel role or relationship.
Key point: Agent and distributor are different channel roles because their commercial responsibilities differ.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
22. Q: How should parent organizations, subsidiaries, divisions, and departments be represented?
A: Show answer
These are organization-unit roles that describe an enterprise's internal or external structure. A parent organization encompasses other enterprises; a subsidiary is wholly or partly owned by another organization; a division is a portion dedicated to a purpose; and a department is a more specific organizational unit, sometimes within a division. Representing the unit as an organization and its structural capacity as a role avoids confusing organizational identity with the current position in a hierarchy. The relationships between units then express which unit contains or governs another and when that structure is valid.
Study instruction: Draw a parent company with two subsidiaries, one division, and two departments. Mark each node as an organization and each structural capacity as a role, then connect the hierarchy with dated relationships.
Key point: Organization identity and organizational placement are separate modeling concerns.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
23. Q: What is the purpose of ROLE TYPE and its subtypes?
A: Show answer
ROLE TYPE provides a common catalogue structure for the kinds of roles that parties may perform. PARTY ROLE TYPE is one specialization, while other business areas can define ORDER ROLE TYPE, SHIPMENT ROLE TYPE, INVOICE ROLE TYPE, and other transaction-specific role types. This shared pattern gives role types common identifiers and descriptions while allowing each process to maintain its own vocabulary. The model's diagrams may omit repeated supertype details for readability, but the underlying design principle is that role types across subject areas can share a common structure.
Study instruction: Create a small ROLE TYPE hierarchy containing party, order, and shipment role types. Identify the common attributes and list the process-specific values that belong to each subtype.
Key point: A shared role-type pattern supports consistent role catalogues across business processes.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
24. Q: Which party roles depend on another party relationship, and which can stand alone?
A: Show answer
Some roles are meaningful only in relation to another party. A PARENT ORGANIZATION role, for example, is meaningful because another organization is its subsidiary. Other roles, such as doctor or notary in the chapter's examples, can be asserted independently without a specific relationship to another party. This distinction determines whether role validity is primarily derived from a PARTY RELATIONSHIP or must be maintained directly on PARTY ROLE. The model allows optional from-date and through-date attributes on PARTY ROLE, particularly useful for roles whose validity is independent of a relationship record.
Study instruction: Classify parent organization, subsidiary, employee, doctor, and notary as relationship-dependent or potentially standalone. Explain which entity should control the effective period for each case.
Key point: A role's lifecycle may be independent or dependent on a relationship, and the model should show which.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
25. Q: Should roles always be inferred from transactions, or can they be declared explicitly?
A: Show answer
Some roles can be inferred from events such as orders, shipments, invoices, or employment records. However, enterprises may need to declare a role before any transaction occurs or even when the underlying transactions are not stored in the system. A prospect may be known before placing an order, and a party may be designated as a customer for operational reasons before a transaction is recorded. Explicit role instances also allow users to find customers, suppliers, or employees without repeatedly searching transaction tables. The design may create a role when a qualifying transaction occurs, but should not assume that all role knowledge is transaction-derived.
Study instruction: For prospect, customer, supplier, employee, and notary, state whether the role can exist before a transaction and identify the event or rule that creates it.
Key point: Roles can be declarative, transaction-derived, or created at transaction time.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
26. Q: What is a PARTY RELATIONSHIP, and how is it different from a role?
A: Show answer
PARTY RELATIONSHIP connects two party-role instances and records how those roles relate to one another. A role says that a party is a customer or supplier; a relationship says whose customer or supplier it is. For example, an organization may be a customer of one subsidiary but not another. Likewise, a person may be the contact for a particular customer account or an employee of a specific internal organization. The relationship therefore supplies context that a standalone role cannot express and is the proper place for facts that belong to that particular pairing.
Study instruction: Write two examples in which a party has the same role but different relationship partners. Identify the two role instances and the relationship record for each example.
Key point: Roles identify capacities; relationships connect those capacities to specific counterparties.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
27. Q: Why is it important to identify the two role participants in a relationship?
A: Show answer
The same party can participate in multiple relationships with different counterparties, and each relationship can have a different business meaning. Knowing only that a person is a customer contact does not identify which organization they represent or which internal organization they interact with. A relationship defined by two role instances makes both ends explicit. It also allows the model to represent relationships among organizations, people and organizations, or people and people using a consistent structure. The subtype or relationship type clarifies the direction and meaning of the pairing.
Study instruction: Model a customer relationship, an employment relationship, and a mentor relationship. For each, label both role participants and explain why swapping the participants would change or invalidate the meaning.
Key point: A relationship must identify both participants and the role each participant plays.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
28. Q: Why should status, priority, notes, and dates often be attached to a party relationship rather than to a contact person?
A: Show answer
Those facts may describe the enterprise's particular relationship with the contact, not the contact as a person. Two sales representatives may interact with the same individual about different product lines and have different relationship statuses, priorities, notes, and start dates. If those facts are stored only on the contact record, one representative's updates can overwrite another's context. A relationship entity allows each business pairing to maintain its own state and history while the shared person record remains consistent. Access rules can still distinguish private relationship notes from enterprise-wide information.
Study instruction: Design two sales relationships with the same contact but different product lines. Assign different priorities and statuses and show why storing them on PERSON would create a conflict.
Key point: Relationship-specific information belongs to the relationship, not automatically to the shared contact identity.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
29. Q: How do from-date and through-date attributes support party relationships?
A: Show answer
They record the period during which the relationship is valid. A customer relationship may begin when an organization starts buying from an internal organization and end when that relationship ceases. Employment may begin and end with a particular internal organization. Temporal attributes also make it possible to represent changes in organizational hierarchy, such as a department moving from one division to another. The model should distinguish an unknown end date from a known end date and define how adjacent or overlapping periods are interpreted so that historical queries produce unambiguous results.
Study instruction: Create a relationship that begins on one date and ends later. Add a second relationship period after a gap and write rules for determining whether the relationship was active on a specified date.
Key point: Relationship validity is temporal and should not be represented only by a current status flag.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
30. Q: How does CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIP represent the scope of a customer relationship?
A: Show answer
CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIP connects a CUSTOMER role to an INTERNAL ORGANIZATION role. This allows an enterprise to identify not merely that an organization is a customer, but which internal company, subsidiary, or division it is a customer of. The chapter also notes that the model can be broadened by relating customer and supplier roles where the enterprise needs to track customers of partners or competitors. The relationship subtype therefore expresses the business scope explicitly and avoids treating a customer relationship as a global property of the party when it may apply only to one organizational unit.
Study instruction: Create one customer organization that buys from two subsidiaries but not from the parent company. Show the separate customer relationship instances and explain how a query would identify the correct account owner.
Key point: Customer status may be specific to an internal organization, not universal across the enterprise.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
31. Q: How do EMPLOYMENT and ORGANIZATION ROLLUP illustrate different party relationships?
A: Show answer
EMPLOYMENT relates an EMPLOYEE role to an INTERNAL ORGANIZATION role and supports the fact that a person may work for several internal organizations over time, while each organization may have many employees. ORGANIZATION ROLLUP relates organization-unit roles to other organization-unit roles and represents hierarchical placement. The rollup can change over time: a department may move from one division to another, so a fixed parent identifier on the department could lose historical structure. Both examples use the common party-relationship pattern while preserving their own business meaning through specific relationship subtypes.
Study instruction: Model a person who works for two subsidiaries in different periods and a department that moves between divisions. Identify the separate relationship records and the dates needed to reconstruct each history.
Key point: Specialized relationship subtypes reuse a common structure while retaining domain-specific semantics.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
32. Q: What is PARTY RELATIONSHIP TYPE, and how does it constrain valid relationships?
A: Show answer
PARTY RELATIONSHIP TYPE describes the meaning of a relationship and the pair of role types that may participate in it. A customer relationship, for example, is defined for a customer role and an internal-organization role. The relationship type's name and description explain the business meaning, while its links to the two PARTY ROLE TYPE values define the permitted participants. This prevents a generic relationship table from becoming an ungoverned collection of arbitrary role pairings. The enterprise should document whether the relationship is directional and which role occupies each endpoint.
Study instruction: Create a relationship-type catalogue for customer, supplier, employment, and organization rollup. For each, specify the two allowed role types, direction, and a plain-language definition.
Key point: Relationship types define the permitted role pair and the meaning of the connection.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
33. Q: How should the model handle a relationship type that can connect more than one possible role subtype?
A: Show answer
If a business relationship may use different combinations of role subtypes, the model must make those combinations explicit. The chapter discusses alternatives such as defining separate person-client and organization-client roles or allowing a client role whose PARTY subtype identifies whether it is a person or organization. If the enterprise needs multiple combinations under one relationship concept, PARTY RELATIONSHIP TYPE may need its own identifier and a many-to-many association to the permitted PARTY ROLE TYPE values. The correct design depends on whether each role pair uniquely identifies the relationship type or whether one type permits several valid pairs.
Study instruction: Design a client relationship that may connect either a person client or an organization client to an internal organization. Compare separate relationship types with one flexible type and state the integrity rules each design requires.
Key point: Model role-pair flexibility deliberately; do not assume one relationship type always maps to one fixed pair.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
34. Q: When should PARTY RELATIONSHIP TYPE be included in the key of PARTY RELATIONSHIP?
A: Show answer
If the two role instances uniquely identify one relationship, the relationship type may not need to be part of the relationship's unique identifier. If the same role pair can participate in more than one distinct relationship type, the type must be represented in the identifier or another explicit uniqueness strategy must distinguish the instances. This is a business-key decision: it depends on the allowed combinations and multiplicity, not simply on diagram convenience. The physical design should also enforce primary-key and foreign-key constraints so that each relationship references valid role instances.
Study instruction: Construct two cases: one in which a role pair can have only one relationship and another in which the same pair can have two relationship types. Propose a primary or alternate key for each and test whether it prevents collisions.
Key point: Relationship uniqueness must reflect the actual permitted multiplicity of role pairings.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
Microsoft: Database Design Basics
SAP PowerDesigner: Primary, Alternate, and Foreign Keys
35. Q: What information can be maintained about a party relationship beyond its participants?
A: Show answer
The model can associate a relationship with a PRIORITY TYPE, a PARTY RELATIONSHIP STATUS TYPE, and one or more COMMUNICATION EVENT records. Priority indicates the relative importance of the relationship to the enterprise, while status describes its state, such as active, inactive, or pursuing greater involvement. Communication events provide the history of interactions within that relationship. These facts should be maintained at relationship level because they may differ between two relationships involving the same party. The enterprise should define controlled values and clear business meanings so that priority and status are not used interchangeably.
Study instruction: For three relationships, assign a priority, a status, and at least one communication event. Write definitions for each priority and status value so that different users would classify the same situation consistently.
Key point: Priority, status, and interactions enrich the specific relationship rather than the party globally.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
36. Q: Why does the book use a common ROLE TYPE pattern for transaction participants?
A: Show answer
Parties can play roles not only in ongoing enterprise relationships but also in individual transactions. An order may have a party placing it, giving it, or paying for it; a shipment may have sender and receiver roles; an invoice may have other participants. A common ROLE TYPE pattern allows these transaction-specific role catalogues to share a structure while retaining their own permitted values. This makes the enterprise model more consistent and supports reuse of role concepts across orders, shipments, invoices, and other subject areas without confusing a transaction role with a long-lived party role.
Study instruction: For an order and a shipment, list the participant roles and connect each role instance to PARTY. Identify which role types are specific to the transaction and which are general party roles.
Key point: Transaction roles describe participation in a particular business object, not necessarily a permanent party capacity.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
37. Q: Why should postal addresses be modeled as entities instead of as fixed attributes of PERSON or ORGANIZATION?
A: Show answer
A party may have several addresses, and one address may be shared by several parties. An address may also have its own descriptive information, such as directions, that should not be repeated for every party using it. Fixed address columns on PERSON or ORGANIZATION make it difficult to represent multiple home, work, mailing, service, or shared addresses and encourage users to place overflow information in comments. A POSTAL ADDRESS entity centralizes the address details so they can be reused and maintained consistently, while an association records which parties use each address.
Study instruction: Create a scenario with one company at three locations and two subsidiaries sharing a mailing address. Compare a fixed-address-column design with a separate POSTAL ADDRESS entity and identify the update anomalies avoided.
Key point: An address is a reusable, potentially multi-valued object with its own descriptive information.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
38. Q: Why is PARTY POSTAL ADDRESS an associative entity?
A: Show answer
The relationship between PARTY and POSTAL ADDRESS is many-to-many. A person can have home, work, and vacation addresses, while one address can be associated with many people or organizations, such as employees at a shared facility or subsidiaries using a common mailing address. PARTY POSTAL ADDRESS resolves this many-to-many relationship by linking the party identifier to the address identifier. It can also hold facts about the association, including the period during which the party used the address. This prevents address details from being copied into each party record and allows the same address to be reused.
Study instruction: Draw the PARTY-to-POSTAL-ADDRESS many-to-many relationship and resolve it with PARTY POSTAL ADDRESS. Add sample rows showing one party with two addresses and one address shared by two parties.
Key point: The associative entity stores the party-address association, not a duplicate address.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
Microsoft: Database Design Basics
39. Q: How can address history be preserved when a party moves?
A: Show answer
The association between a party and an address includes from-date and through-date attributes. When a party moves, the previous association can be closed and a new association created, rather than overwriting the party's old address or deleting the address record. This distinguishes the address itself from the period during which a party used it. The same address may remain valid for another party after the first party leaves. Historical address use can support correspondence research, transaction reconstruction, and operational analysis, subject to the enterprise's retention and privacy rules.
Study instruction: Model a person who moves twice and an organization that shares one address with another organization. Close each association at the appropriate date and demonstrate how to retrieve the address valid on a past date.
Key point: Address history belongs on the party-address association and should not be lost through overwriting.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
40. Q: What is the role of GEOGRAPHIC BOUNDARY in the postal address model?
A: Show answer
GEOGRAPHIC BOUNDARY represents areas that contain or describe addresses, such as city, county, state, country, province, territory, postal code, sales territory, service territory, or region. It separates geographic concepts from the free-form address lines and allows the enterprise to associate addresses with multiple relevant boundaries. A postal code supports postal sorting and delivery, while a sales or service territory supports business operations. The same address may therefore be described by administrative, postal, and enterprise-defined geographic boundaries without treating them as interchangeable concepts.
Study instruction: For one address, list its country, province or state, city, postal code, and sales region. Identify which values are postal or administrative boundaries and which are enterprise-defined territories.
Key point: Geographic boundaries support standardized location context beyond address text lines.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
41. Q: Why are geographic boundaries modeled recursively?
A: Show answer
Geographic areas can contain or be composed of other geographic areas. A region may contain several states or provinces, a state may contain cities, and an enterprise sales territory may be defined by a set of cities or countries. A recursive relationship allows a GEOGRAPHIC BOUNDARY to relate to other instances of the same entity, supporting hierarchies at different levels. This is more flexible than hard-coding one fixed chain of country, state, and city columns. The enterprise must define the hierarchy rules and distinguish containment from other forms of geographic association.
Study instruction: Draw a recursive hierarchy for a service region containing two cities and a separate sales territory containing cities across two states. Explain why a boundary can have different parent groupings for different purposes.
Key point: Recursive boundary relationships represent nested or grouped geographies without fixing one universal hierarchy.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
42. Q: What design alternatives exist for linking addresses to geographic boundaries?
A: Show answer
The chapter presents an associative POSTAL ADDRESS BOUNDARY approach and notes that a more specialized model could instead connect POSTAL ADDRESS directly to specific boundary types, such as CITY or POSTAL CODE. The associative approach is flexible when an address can relate to many boundary categories and when the set of categories may vary. Direct relationships can be simpler when the application has a known, limited geography and needs strongly typed links. A worldwide design must account for different administrative structures, such as provinces, territories, and prefectures, rather than assuming every country follows the same pattern.
Study instruction: Compare the associative design with direct address-to-city and address-to-postal-code relationships. Evaluate extensibility, validation, query complexity, and suitability for a single-country versus global application.
Key point: Choose geographic linkage based on the required scope and variation of geographic structures.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
43. Q: Why is a fixed set of phone, fax, and email columns a weak contact-data design?
A: Show answer
Fixed columns assume that the enterprise knows in advance how many contact values each party will have and which technologies will be used. A party may have several business numbers, multiple email addresses, or new contact channels that were not anticipated when the schema was created. Additional values are often placed in comment fields, making them difficult to validate, search, or use in automated processes. A contact-mechanism model stores each channel as a separate occurrence, supports multiple values, and allows new types to be introduced through reference data rather than by repeatedly adding columns.
Study instruction: Design a contact record for a person with two office numbers, a mobile number, two email addresses, and a web profile. Show why fixed columns become cumbersome and how separate mechanism records solve the problem.
Key point: Contact channels are multi-valued and extensible, so they should not be limited to a few fixed columns.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
44. Q: What are CONTACT MECHANISM, CONTACT MECHANISM TYPE, and their subtypes?
A: Show answer
CONTACT MECHANISM represents a way to reach a party. CONTACT MECHANISM TYPE provides controlled categories such as phone, mobile phone, fax, email address, Internet address, or web URL. The chapter further specializes mechanisms into TELECOMMUNICATIONS NUMBER and ELECTRONIC ADDRESS. This structure separates the actual contact value from its classification and allows new categories to be introduced as technology evolves. A subtype can carry attributes specific to that channel while the common supertype provides a shared reference for party associations and business processes that need any kind of contact method.
Study instruction: Build a small subtype diagram for contact mechanisms. Assign six sample values to the correct subtype and show which attributes belong to the common mechanism versus a specialized subtype.
Key point: A common contact-mechanism abstraction supports multiple channel types and future extensions.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
45. Q: Why is PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM needed between PARTY and CONTACT MECHANISM?
A: Show answer
The association records which party uses or is reachable through which contact mechanism. A single mechanism may be shared or associated with multiple parties, and a party may have many mechanisms. The association can also carry facts that describe the use of that mechanism by that party, such as a non-solicitation indicator or role-specific applicability. Keeping these facts on the association avoids placing them on the contact value itself, where they could incorrectly apply to every party using the same mechanism. It also distinguishes the reusable mechanism from the context in which a particular party uses it.
Study instruction: Model a shared switchboard number used by two related organizations and a mobile number used by one person. Identify which facts belong to CONTACT MECHANISM and which belong to PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM.
Key point: The association captures the party's use of a contact mechanism and its context-specific attributes.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
46. Q: What is the purpose of the non-solicitation indicator on PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM?
A: Show answer
It records that a particular contact mechanism should not be used for solicitation. The chapter emphasizes that this may be important for business considerations and legal obligations. Placing the indicator on the party-to-mechanism association makes it possible for a restriction to apply to one number or address without assuming that all contact channels for the party share the same restriction. Implementations should define how the indicator is interpreted, which communication purposes it governs, how changes are audited, and how downstream campaign or contact systems enforce it before initiating outreach.
Study instruction: Create a party with two phone numbers and one email address, then mark only one phone number as non-solicitation. Write a validation rule that prevents a solicitation event from using the restricted mechanism.
Key point: Contact restrictions can be mechanism-specific and must be enforced at the point of use.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
47. Q: What is gained by modeling POSTAL ADDRESS as a subtype of CONTACT MECHANISM?
A: Show answer
The expanded model treats postal addresses, telecommunications numbers, and electronic addresses as different ways to reach a party. A business process that needs a contact mechanism can then refer to one common concept rather than maintaining separate alternatives for mailing address, phone, or email. This supports flexible contact lists and processes that may accept different channels, such as an order that can be confirmed through a postal or electronic address. The approach also allows postal contact details to participate in the same general association and purpose structures as other contact methods.
Study instruction: Model a notification process that can use either postal mail or email. Show the common contact-mechanism reference and the subtype-specific details required to deliver each notification.
Key point: Treating postal address as a contact subtype unifies processes that can use different delivery channels.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
48. Q: Why might a contact mechanism be specific to a party role?
A: Show answer
An organization may provide one address for its customer role and a different address for its supplier role. A contact mechanism that is correct for one business capacity may be inappropriate for another. The expanded model therefore allows PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM to be associated with PARTY ROLE TYPE when contact applicability depends on role. This prevents a process from assuming that every address or phone number associated with a party is suitable for every interaction. The enterprise should define whether role applicability is mandatory, optional, or inherited from a general party-level contact association.
Study instruction: Give one organization separate customer billing, supplier remittance, and general headquarters contacts. Assign each mechanism to the appropriate role and show which contact is selected for each process.
Key point: Contact applicability may be role-specific even when party identity is shared.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
49. Q: What does CONTACT MECHANISM LINK represent?
A: Show answer
CONTACT MECHANISM LINK relates one contact mechanism to another when there is an operational relationship between them. For example, a phone number may route to a pager or mobile number when busy, or a fax mechanism may be associated with an email address for delivery handling. The link allows the system to record how one contact channel relates to or redirects toward another without embedding routing logic in the party record. Implementations should define the direction, link type, validity period, and whether a link is informational or actively used by communication processes.
Study instruction: Draw a main telephone number linked to an after-hours mobile number and a fax-to-email arrangement. Label the link meaning and identify any validity dates needed when routing arrangements change.
Key point: Contact-mechanism links capture relationships between channels, not merely additional contact values.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
50. Q: Why should contact mechanism purpose be modeled separately from the party-contact association?
A: Show answer
A single address or number may serve several purposes. One postal address might be used for headquarters, mailing, service, and billing inquiries; one phone number might support both voice and fax. If each purpose creates a separate PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM row, attributes that describe the association itself—such as a non-solicitation indicator—would be repeated. A separate PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM PURPOSE entity allows one party-mechanism association to have multiple purposes while preserving attributes that belong to the association only once. CONTACT MECHANISM PURPOSE TYPE supplies the controlled purpose vocabulary.
Study instruction: Use one address for headquarters, mailing, and billing. Compare a design that duplicates the party-mechanism row with one that uses three purpose rows and identify which attributes would otherwise be repeated.
Key point: Separate purpose occurrences from the underlying party-to-mechanism association to avoid duplication.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
51. Q: How should changes in the purpose of a contact mechanism be recorded?
A: Show answer
The model uses from-date and through-date attributes on PARTY CONTACT MECHANISM PURPOSE to show when a purpose is valid. An address may be the billing address during one period and later become only a service address. Keeping purpose history separate from the contact value and the party-mechanism association allows the enterprise to preserve earlier usage without creating duplicate copies of the address. The enterprise should define whether multiple purposes may overlap, how expired purposes are closed, and which purpose takes precedence when a process requires one selected contact channel.
Study instruction: Create a timeline in which an address begins as a billing address, later becomes a service address, and then ceases to be used. Represent each purpose period and test retrieval for three different dates.
Key point: Purpose is time-dependent and should be tracked as a dated association.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
52. Q: What is the difference between a FACILITY and a CONTACT MECHANISM?
A: Show answer
FACILITY represents a physical structure or place, such as a warehouse, plant, building, room, or office. CONTACT MECHANISM represents a way to reach a party or location, such as a telephone number, email address, or postal address. A plant may have several contact mechanisms, but the phone number is not the plant itself. Likewise, a facility can have physical characteristics and relationships—such as area, occupancy, or ownership—that do not belong to the contact value. Separating the concepts prevents physical assets and communication identifiers from being conflated.
Study instruction: Model a manufacturing plant with a street address, postal box, phone number, and email address. Identify the FACILITY record, each CONTACT MECHANISM, and the associations connecting them.
Key point: FACILITY describes the physical place; CONTACT MECHANISM describes how it can be contacted.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
53. Q: How can facilities be organized into a physical hierarchy?
A: Show answer
FACILITY can have subtypes such as WAREHOUSE, PLANT, BUILDING, ROOM, and OFFICE, with FACILITY TYPE providing a way to classify additional kinds. A facility may be composed of other facilities: a building may contain floors and rooms, while a plant may contain buildings or other operational areas. This recursive structure allows the enterprise to represent the physical granularity it needs without forcing every organization to use the same levels. Attributes such as square footage can be maintained at the facility level where they are meaningful.
Study instruction: Draw a plant containing two buildings, each with floors and rooms. Identify which levels are necessary for a simple property register and which would be needed for maintenance or space-management applications.
Key point: Recursive facility composition supports physical hierarchies at the required level of detail.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
54. Q: What does FACILITY ROLE contribute to facility modeling?
A: Show answer
A facility may involve one or more parties in different capacities. One party may own it, another may lease it, and others may use or rent it. FACILITY ROLE and FACILITY ROLE TYPE represent those capacities explicitly instead of adding fixed owner, tenant, or user columns to FACILITY. This supports multiple parties and changing responsibilities over time. The role model also makes it possible to add other facility-related responsibilities without redesigning the core facility entity, provided the enterprise defines the allowed role types and their business rules.
Study instruction: Model a warehouse owned by one organization, leased by another, and operated by a third. Identify the facility, the three parties, and their distinct facility roles.
Key point: Facility roles describe who owns, leases, rents, or uses a physical facility.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
55. Q: Why can FACILITY CONTACT MECHANISM be many-to-many?
A: Show answer
A facility may have several contact mechanisms, including a street address, postal box, phone number, fax number, and email address. A contact mechanism may also be shared by multiple facilities, such as a common address serving several plants in one complex. The associative FACILITY CONTACT MECHANISM entity supports both possibilities and can hold any facts that describe the association. This avoids assuming that every contact value belongs to exactly one facility or that every facility has exactly one contact method.
Study instruction: Create two facilities that share one postal address but have different phone numbers. Draw the associative entity and show the rows needed to represent both facilities accurately.
Key point: Facility-to-contact links must accommodate shared mechanisms and multiple mechanisms per facility.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
56. Q: What is a COMMUNICATION EVENT, and what business information should it preserve?
A: Show answer
COMMUNICATION EVENT records an interchange of information between parties through a channel such as a phone call, meeting, videoconference, letter, or email. It provides a history of communications that have occurred or are planned. The event can record start and end date-times, status, notes, the contact mechanism type, and its purpose. This history helps sales, service, purchasing, and other teams understand what was discussed, when it happened, and what action may be needed. It is more structured than a free-text note attached to a contact because the event has its own identity and relationships.
Study instruction: Design an event record for a customer support call and a sales meeting. Identify the fields needed to answer who communicated, when, through which channel, for what purpose, and with what outcome.
Key point: A communication event is a traceable business occurrence with time, channel, purpose, and participants.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
57. Q: When should a communication event be associated with PARTY RELATIONSHIP rather than only with event participants?
A: Show answer
Most communication events make sense within the context of a particular relationship. Two parties may have more than one relationship over time—for example, a person may first be a customer contact and later become an employee or manager within an organization. Recording the event against the relevant PARTY RELATIONSHIP keeps the communication history attached to the correct business context. For events involving several parties or where a single relationship is not the appropriate context, COMMUNICATION EVENT ROLE can identify each participant and the role they played in the event.
Study instruction: Model two parties who first interact as customer and account representative and later as manager and employee. Place separate communication events in the correct relationship context and explain when event roles are needed instead.
Key point: Communication history should be linked to the relationship context it concerns, with event roles for broader participation.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
58. Q: What does COMMUNICATION EVENT ROLE add to meetings and other multi-party events?
A: Show answer
A communication event may involve more than two parties, as in a meeting, conference, or seminar. COMMUNICATION EVENT ROLE identifies the parties participating and the roles they perform, such as facilitator, participant, or note taker. It avoids limiting the event to a single caller and receiver pair and allows the same event to have several participants with different responsibilities. The model can validate which event roles are appropriate for a particular contact mechanism type through VALID CONTACT MECHANISM ROLE, such as caller and receiver for a phone call or facilitator and participant for a face-to-face meeting.
Study instruction: Model a meeting with a facilitator, three participants, and a note taker. Then model a phone call with caller and receiver roles and compare the participant structures.
Key point: Event roles describe each participant's function within a multi-party communication.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
59. Q: Why should a communication event's channel, purpose, and status be modeled separately?
A: Show answer
These attributes answer different questions. The contact mechanism type records how the communication occurred, such as phone, email, or face-to-face. Communication event purpose records why it occurred, such as a support call, sales follow-up, inquiry, meeting, or seminar. Status records the event's lifecycle state, such as scheduled, in progress, or completed. One event has one channel in the chapter's model but may have several purposes; for example, a meeting can address customer support and an additional delivery request. Keeping these dimensions separate avoids overloaded codes and supports more useful reporting.
Study instruction: Classify five sample events by channel, one or more purposes, and status. Include a meeting with two purposes and explain why those purposes should not be encoded as separate communication channels.
Key point: Channel, purpose, and lifecycle status are independent dimensions of an event.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
60. Q: How do CASE and WORK EFFORT support communication-event follow-up?
A: Show answer
A CASE groups related communication events concerning one issue, while CASE ROLE identifies the parties responsible for the case, monitoring service quality, acting as customer, or performing other case responsibilities. WORK EFFORT represents work required as a result of an event. One communication event may create several work efforts, and one work effort may be discussed across several communication events. This structure connects customer or supplier conversations to operational action and follow-up, instead of leaving requests as untracked notes. It also allows a case to remain open while several events and tasks contribute to resolving the underlying issue.
Study instruction: Build a support case for a software problem. Add the initial call, a work effort to send a patch, an email confirming delivery, and a final call verifying resolution. Identify case roles and work-effort links.
Key point: CASE groups related events; WORK EFFORT tracks the actions needed to resolve them.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
61. Q: Why is the relationship between COMMUNICATION EVENT and WORK EFFORT many-to-many?
A: Show answer
A single communication can generate several actions—for example, investigate an issue, send a software patch, and arrange a training session. Conversely, one work effort may be requested in one event, discussed in later calls, and confirmed in a final email. A many-to-many association preserves all of these links without duplicating the event or work-effort records. It also makes it possible to trace why work was initiated and which communications reported progress or completion. The association can be extended with link-specific details if the business needs to distinguish requested, updated, or completed relationships.
Study instruction: Create two communication events and two work efforts where one event creates both work efforts and one work effort is referenced by both events. Draw the associative structure and explain what each link means.
Key point: Events and work efforts have independent identities and can be connected in both directions.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
62. Q: How can the complete communication follow-up lifecycle be represented without losing accountability?
A: Show answer
A robust lifecycle links the initiating communication to a case, assigns case roles, creates one or more work efforts, records subsequent communications about those efforts, and closes the case only when the required outcome is confirmed. The initial event explains why work began; the work effort identifies the action and its responsibility; later events document progress and customer contact. Status and date information should make it possible to distinguish scheduled, active, completed, and unresolved work. The enterprise should define closure criteria and ensure that a completed communication does not automatically imply that the underlying work has been completed.
Study instruction: Write a step-by-step process for a service issue from first call to closure. At each step identify the entity updated, responsible role, status transition, and evidence required before closure.
Key point: Follow-up accountability requires traceable links between communications, cases, work, and verified outcomes.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
63. Q: What are the most important implementation decisions when adapting this model to an enterprise?
A: Show answer
The model is a general foundation and should be customized to the enterprise's business rules, scale, data availability, and application needs. Important decisions include which party attributes are genuinely common, which repeated attributes require history entities, which roles can exist independently, which relationship types and role pairs are valid, how temporal periods are represented, whether addresses and contact mechanisms are reusable, and how communication events connect to cases and work. The enterprise should also define identity-matching rules, reference-data ownership, privacy controls for sensitive attributes, and validation rules that prevent contradictory or duplicate records. A design should be tested against real business scenarios before it is implemented.
Study instruction: Prepare an implementation checklist for a customer-management system using this model. Include identity, role, relationship, contact, temporal, security, and data-quality decisions, and test the checklist against at least three realistic scenarios.
Key point: Reuse the common model, but validate every structure against actual enterprise rules and use cases.
Source links: Silverston, The Data Model Resource Book: People and Organizations
Rows: 63
Table 3
Enterprise Product Information Model — Study Reference
1. Q: What does the enterprise product model define as a product?
A: Show answer
A product is a good or service that an enterprise has sold, currently sells, or expects to sell. The model is intended to capture the reusable identity and descriptive information of those offerings, not merely the items currently stocked or sold by one business unit. Its scope therefore includes current, future, and discontinued offerings and supports operational, commercial, and analytical use.
Study instruction: Write a one-sentence product definition, then classify five examples as current, future, or discontinued offerings. Explain why a product record may remain useful after sales stop.
Key point: Model the identity of an offering across its lifecycle, not just today's sales inventory.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
2. Q: How does the model distinguish goods from services?
A: Show answer
A GOOD represents a more tangible offering that can generally be physically stored, such as stationery, furniture, or equipment. A SERVICE represents an offering in which a party's time or expertise is sold, such as consulting or legal work. The distinction affects operational treatment: goods commonly require inventory, storage, and reorder controls, while services are often measured and priced by time, usage, or deliverables.
Study instruction: Classify examples from a retailer, manufacturer, and professional-services firm. For each, state whether physical inventory, time-based measurement, or both are relevant.
Key point: Goods are tangible stockable offerings; services primarily sell time or expertise.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
3. Q: Why does the model use a common PRODUCT supertype for an enterprise's own, supplier, and competitor products?
A: Show answer
A common PRODUCT entity stores shared product identity and descriptive facts once, regardless of which organization sells or supplies the offering. This avoids creating separate product definitions for the enterprise, each supplier, and each competitor. It also allows common category, feature, and association structures to be reused, while organization-dependent facts such as price and availability are recorded in relationships that carry the relevant organization context.
Study instruction: Sketch one PRODUCT entity connected to three organizations in different roles. Mark which attributes belong to PRODUCT and which belong to the organization-product relationship.
Key point: Separate product identity from the commercial party offering it.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
4. Q: Which core attributes describe the lifecycle of a product?
A: Show answer
The chapter identifies a product identifier, name, introduction date, sales discontinuation date, support discontinuation date, and comment. These attributes answer different questions: when the offering first became available, when it ceased to be sold, and when manufacturer support ended. Sales and support can end at different times, so a single generic end date would lose important lifecycle meaning.
Study instruction: Create a sample product record with different sales and support end dates. Explain what operational decisions each date should influence.
Key point: Introduction, sales end, and support end are distinct lifecycle events.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
5. Q: Which product facts are independent of the supplier, and which depend on the supplier?
A: Show answer
Descriptions, categories, and many product features can describe the product regardless of who offers it. Availability, lead time, and price may differ by supplier or selling organization. The model therefore keeps common descriptive information with PRODUCT and stores organization-specific offering information in a separate associative structure such as SUPPLIER PRODUCT or PRICE COMPONENT.
Study instruction: For a product sold by the enterprise and two resellers, sort ten sample facts into product-level facts and organization-specific offering facts. Explain any borderline cases.
Key point: Store stable product facts once and contextual commercial facts with the offering relationship.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
6. Q: Why are product categories modeled as reusable entities rather than hard-coded labels on PRODUCT?
A: Show answer
Products may be classified by product line, model, grade, market segment, function, or other business groupings. A separate PRODUCT CATEGORY supertype lets other structures, such as pricing and market-interest analysis, relate to categories without depending on one specific classification scheme. This makes category definitions reusable and allows the enterprise to introduce new classification purposes without redesigning every dependent entity.
Study instruction: List four independent category schemes for one product catalogue. Identify which downstream processes should be able to reference each scheme.
Key point: A category is a reusable classification concept, not merely a display label.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
7. Q: Why is PRODUCT CATEGORY CLASSIFICATION an associative entity?
A: Show answer
A product may belong to several categories, and a category may contain many products. PRODUCT CATEGORY CLASSIFICATION resolves this many-to-many relationship and records each product-to-category membership. It can also carry relationship-specific attributes, such as effective dates and a primary-category indicator, that do not belong naturally to PRODUCT or PRODUCT CATEGORY alone.
Study instruction: Draw the many-to-many relationship and populate it with a product assigned to two categories and a category containing several products. Identify the attributes that belong on the intersection.
Key point: Use an associative entity when the relationship itself has business meaning or attributes.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
8. Q: Why does product-category membership need from-date and thru-date attributes?
A: Show answer
Classification can change over time. Effective dates preserve when a product belonged to a category, allowing historical reports to use the classification that applied at the time rather than today's category structure. Without temporal membership, a product moved to a new category could make prior sales analyses appear as though the new classification had always applied.
Study instruction: Model a product that moves from one category to another on a known date. Write a query requirement for both current classification and classification as of a past reporting date.
Key point: Category membership is time-dependent and should be historically reconstructable.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
9. Q: What problem does PRODUCT CATEGORY ROLLUP solve?
A: Show answer
The recursive PRODUCT CATEGORY ROLLUP relationship allows categories to contain subcategories and permits a subcategory to participate under more than one parent. For example, a paper category may roll up under office supplies and computer supplies. This supports hierarchical navigation and multiple catalog views without duplicating the underlying product definition.
Study instruction: Build a three-level category hierarchy and place one subcategory beneath two parents. Identify how a query should avoid treating the same product as two distinct products.
Key point: A recursive category relationship represents hierarchy while allowing multiple parent paths.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
10. Q: How does MARKET INTEREST support prospecting and sales forecasting?
A: Show answer
MARKET INTEREST links PARTY TYPE to PRODUCT CATEGORY so the enterprise can record which categories may interest particular types of parties. If party types represent industries or market segments, the organization can identify actual parties within those segments and target them with relevant campaigns. From-date and thru-date attributes preserve changes in interest over time.
Study instruction: Create a prospecting example linking an industry party type to two product categories. Show how the target list would change when the interest period expires.
Key point: Market interest connects target-party segments to product-category demand signals.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
11. Q: Why can assigning one product to multiple categories overstate sales totals?
A: Show answer
A sales report grouped by category may count the same product's sales once in every category to which it belongs. Adding those category totals can therefore exceed actual enterprise sales. The chapter proposes a primary-category flag to identify the category used for non-duplicative analysis, with a business rule that only one classification per product may be primary for that purpose.
Study instruction: Create a small sales dataset in which one product belongs to two categories. Calculate the naive category total and compare it with the total using one primary category.
Key point: Multi-category membership is useful, but additive reporting needs an explicit counting rule.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
12. Q: When is a PRODUCT CLASSIFICATION TYPE entity preferable to a single primary-category flag?
A: Show answer
A single primary flag assumes there is one universally primary category. If the primary category depends on the application, such as a primary category for catalogues versus one for sales analysis, the classification relationship needs a type that identifies the purpose of the primary designation. This preserves multiple valid primary classifications without forcing one business context to govern all others.
Study instruction: Define three classification purposes and assign a different primary category for each. Explain why a single Boolean flag cannot represent all three decisions.
Key point: Primary status may be purpose-specific rather than globally unique.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
13. Q: Why does GOOD IDENTIFICATION store multiple identification codes for one good?
A: Show answer
A good can be known by several identifiers used by different organizations or processes. The chapter gives manufacturer identification numbers, SKUs, UPC formats, and ISBNs as examples. GOOD IDENTIFICATION stores the code value, while subtypes identify the kind of code. This avoids assuming that one enterprise key is the only identifier used across manufacturers, retailers, and standards bodies.
Study instruction: For one physical good, record an internal product ID, manufacturer code, retailer SKU, and applicable trade-item identifier. State the assigning authority and intended use of each.
Key point: A product's internal key and its external identification codes serve different purposes.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
14. Q: How should a data model distinguish a manufacturer number, SKU, GTIN, and ISBN?
A: Show answer
These identifiers are not interchangeable. A manufacturer number is assigned by the manufacturer, an SKU is an identifier used by a particular stock-keeping organization, a GTIN is a standardized trade-item identifier used across supply chains, and an ISBN identifies a book publication. The model should record identifier type and value, preserve the assigning authority or namespace where needed, and avoid assuming that a code is globally unique merely because it is unique within one retailer.
Study instruction: Prepare a comparison table for four identifiers, including issuer, scope, format rules, and whether the identifier is internal or interoperable across organizations.
Key point: Identifier type and issuing namespace are essential to interpreting a code correctly.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description; GS1: Identification Keys; International ISBN Agency
15. Q: What identifier-standard caution should be applied when implementing the chapter's examples?
A: Show answer
The chapter's code examples are illustrative and should be checked against current standards before implementation. In particular, its expansion of UPC-E as a European Universal Product Code is inaccurate: GS1 describes UPC-E as a compressed representation of a GTIN-12, not a European code. A production model should store the correct business identifier and separately handle barcode symbology or display representation where necessary.
Study instruction: Review the identifier terminology in a proposed schema against current GS1 documentation. Record any difference between the business identifier, its encoded barcode form, and its human-readable display.
Key point: Do not copy historical code labels without validating the current standard.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description; GS1: RFID and Barcode Interoperability Guidelines
16. Q: Why does the model use PRODUCT FEATURE for characteristics, options, and modifiers?
A: Show answer
The same feature may be mandatory for one product, included by default in another, and selectable for a third. Separating required features from optional features into unrelated entities would duplicate concepts and make it difficult to reflect changes in product configuration over time. A common PRODUCT FEATURE structure allows the feature itself to be defined once and its role for a particular product to be recorded through applicability.
Study instruction: Choose one feature, such as white colour, and show how it can be required for one product and optional for another. Identify the shared feature definition and the product-specific applicability.
Key point: A feature's definition can be reused even when its role differs by product.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
17. Q: What does PRODUCT FEATURE APPLICABILITY represent?
A: Show answer
PRODUCT FEATURE APPLICABILITY records which features may apply to which products. Because a feature can be reused across many products and each product can have many features, this is another many-to-many relationship. The intersection is the natural place to store product-specific applicability details rather than embedding a long list of feature columns in PRODUCT.
Study instruction: Draw the product-feature many-to-many relationship. Add two products sharing a feature and one product with several features, then identify relationship attributes that may vary by product.
Key point: Feature applicability belongs to the product-feature relationship.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
18. Q: Why is PRODUCT FEATURE CATEGORY useful?
A: Show answer
PRODUCT FEATURE CATEGORY groups features into concepts such as quality, colour, size, dimension, or style. It allows an enterprise to organize feature definitions and support consistent selection, validation, and reporting. Categories also help user interfaces present related options together without requiring every application to understand each individual feature as a unique structural attribute.
Study instruction: Create a feature catalogue with at least four feature categories and three example values in each. Check whether two departments would classify the same feature consistently.
Key point: Feature categories make a flexible feature catalogue understandable and governable.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
19. Q: How do STANDARD, REQUIRED, SELECTABLE, and OPTIONAL features differ?
A: Show answer
A STANDARD FEATURE comes with the product configuration by default but may be deselected. A REQUIRED FEATURE must be included. A SELECTABLE FEATURE requires a choice, such as selecting a colour. An OPTIONAL FEATURE is an additional component that may be added. These distinctions describe configuration behavior and should not be collapsed into a generic optional flag.
Study instruction: Classify five configuration examples using the four feature roles. For each, state whether a user may remove it, must choose a value, or may add it independently.
Key point: Feature subtype expresses the rule governing a feature's presence in a product configuration.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
20. Q: How should required features be used to describe a specific product offering?
A: Show answer
Required features can define the characteristics that make an offering what it is. In the chapter's paper example, brand, grade, dimensions, colour, and paper type are required characteristics of the specifically named grey bond-paper product. These features make the product identifiable and categorizable, while other available variants can remain selectable or optional rather than being embedded in every product name.
Study instruction: Model a named product with four required characteristics and two optional enhancements. Explain which facts define the offering and which can be chosen at order time.
Key point: Required features define the offering; optional features configure it.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
21. Q: How does PRODUCT FEATURE INTERACTION represent configuration constraints?
A: Show answer
Some features cannot coexist, while others are valid only when a prerequisite feature is selected. PRODUCT FEATURE INTERACTION stores these rules through subtypes such as SELECTION INTERACTION INCOMPATIBILITY and FEATURE INTERACTION DEPENDENCY. This allows the enterprise to validate a configuration before accepting an order rather than relying on users to remember every combination rule.
Study instruction: Write one incompatibility rule and one dependency rule for a laptop configuration. Convert each into a clear validation condition and test valid and invalid selections.
Key point: Feature configuration requires explicit dependency and incompatibility rules.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
22. Q: When should a feature variation be modeled as a separate PRODUCT rather than as a selectable feature?
A: Show answer
The chapter allows products to be defined at multiple levels of specificity. A variation may be represented as a feature when the enterprise wants a configurable offering, but it may be a separate product when the variation is independently marketed, ordered, stocked, priced, or otherwise managed as a distinct offering. The decision should reflect business identity and operational consequences, not just a preference for fewer records.
Study instruction: Compare two colours of the same item. Decide whether colour is an option or a distinct product by testing catalog, pricing, inventory, ordering, and identifier requirements.
Key point: Model a variation as a separate product when the business manages it as a distinct offering.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
23. Q: Why should PRODUCT FEATURE subtypes be customized for the enterprise?
A: Show answer
The chapter's examples include quality, colour, dimension, size, brand name, software features, hardware features, and billing features, but relevant feature types vary by industry. Shoe manufacturers may need style, clothing businesses may need product lines, and commodity businesses may need varieties. The baseline model is therefore a starting point; subtype design should reflect actual business vocabulary and validation needs.
Study instruction: Interview representatives from two business areas and list their meaningful product characteristics. Separate common feature types from industry-specific types and justify each proposed subtype.
Key point: Reuse a common feature framework, but tailor its vocabulary and subtypes to the business.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
24. Q: Why is UNIT OF MEASURE modeled separately from PRODUCT FEATURE?
A: Show answer
The chapter treats the unit in which a product is sold as a separate concept because a piece of paper and a ream of paper may be different products, not merely different values of one descriptive feature. UNIT OF MEASURE also supports standardized measurement and conversion. Keeping it separate avoids mixing a commercial packaging unit with descriptive characteristics such as colour or quality.
Study instruction: Compare a product sold by each, box, and case with a product whose dimensions are width and length. Decide which facts are units of measure and which are descriptive features.
Key point: A sales or inventory unit is not automatically a product feature.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
25. Q: How does UNIT OF MEASURE CONVERSION support inventory and sales aggregation?
A: Show answer
UNIT OF MEASURE CONVERSION relates units through a conversion factor so quantities can be expressed in a common unit. For example, a small box may contain 12 pencils and a large box 24 pencils. Converting both to individual pencils allows the enterprise to aggregate stock, cost, and sales across packaging units. Conversion direction and base-unit conventions must be defined consistently.
Study instruction: Choose a base unit and calculate equivalent quantities for three package sizes. Test that conversions in both directions are consistent and that reports aggregate only compatible measures.
Key point: A common unit and controlled conversion factors make quantity comparisons meaningful.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
26. Q: What does SUPPLIER PRODUCT represent?
A: Show answer
SUPPLIER PRODUCT associates products with the organizations that offer them. It handles the many-to-many reality that one organization may offer many products and one product may be available from several organizations. The same structure can represent the enterprise's own offerings, supplier offerings, and competitor offerings, enabling sourcing and competitive analysis without duplicating PRODUCT definitions.
Study instruction: Create a product offered by the enterprise and two suppliers. Identify the relationship key and the organization-specific facts that belong on each offering record.
Key point: The offering relationship identifies who offers a shared product.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
27. Q: Why are supplier availability dates and lead time recorded on the supplier-product relationship?
A: Show answer
A supplier may offer a product only during a defined period, and its delivery lead time may differ from other suppliers. Available-from and available-through dates preserve when the offer is valid, while standard lead time captures the supplier's quoted delivery expectation. Actual lead time can later be derived from orders and shipments, but the quoted standard is useful for planning and comparison.
Study instruction: Compare two suppliers for the same product using availability windows and quoted lead times. Identify which supplier is eligible for an order on a given date.
Key point: Availability and lead time describe a particular supplier's offer, not the product universally.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
28. Q: How do supplier preference and rating serve different purposes?
A: Show answer
PREFERENCE TYPE records the order in which the enterprise prefers to source a product from alternative suppliers. RATING TYPE records an assessment of the supplier's performance for that product. Preference is a sourcing priority, while rating is an evaluation result; a highly rated supplier is not necessarily first choice if price, capacity, geography, or contractual constraints differ.
Study instruction: Create three supplier offers with separate preference ranks and performance ratings. Explain a business scenario in which the preferred supplier is not selected for a particular order.
Key point: Preference rank and supplier performance rating are distinct decision attributes.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
29. Q: What does REORDER GUIDELINE capture, and where may it vary?
A: Show answer
REORDER GUIDELINE stores a reorder level and recommended reorder quantity for a good. The threshold indicates when replenishment should begin, while the quantity indicates how much to order or reproduce. Guidelines may differ by geographic boundary, facility, or internal organization. The chapter notes that these rules are generally applied to goods rather than services and may support vendor-managed replenishment as well as internal purchasing.
Study instruction: For one stocked good, define different reorder levels for a central warehouse and a regional facility. Explain how the system should select the applicable guideline.
Key point: Replenishment thresholds and quantities are contextual policies, not universal product attributes.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
30. Q: How does the model distinguish a manufacturer from a supplier or subcontractor?
A: Show answer
A supplier is an organization from which the enterprise obtains an offering; a manufacturer is the organization considered responsible for producing the product. A manufacturer may subcontract physical production to another organization and still remain the manufacturer because it retains responsibility for the product. The data model should therefore avoid assuming that the party shipping or physically assembling an item is always its manufacturer.
Study instruction: Draw a supply chain in which a brand owner hires a contract manufacturer and a distributor. Assign manufacturer and supplier roles separately and explain which organization is accountable for the product definition.
Key point: Manufacturing responsibility and supply-chain fulfilment are different roles.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
31. Q: What is the difference between GOOD and INVENTORY ITEM?
A: Show answer
GOOD represents the catalogued product type that can be purchased or sold. INVENTORY ITEM represents a physical occurrence or tracked quantity of that good at a location. One GOOD may therefore have multiple INVENTORY ITEM records across facilities, containers, owners, or lots. This separation allows a stable product definition to exist independently of where and how much stock is currently held.
Study instruction: Model one catalogued paper product with inventory at two warehouses and one copier tracked individually. Identify which attributes belong to GOOD and which belong to INVENTORY ITEM.
Key point: GOOD describes the item type; INVENTORY ITEM describes its physical stock occurrence.
Source links: Wiley: Volume 1 Book Description
32. Q: When should inventory be serialized or non-serialized?
A: Show answer
A SERIALIZED INVENTORY ITEM tracks each individual unit by its own serial number. A NON-SERIALIZED INVENTORY ITEM tracks a group of identical units through a quantity-on-hand value at a location. Serialization is appropriate when individual identity, service history, warranty, or accountability matters; quantity tracking is more practical for interchangeable consumables. The model should make the tracking choice explicit rather than treating every stock record identically.
Study instruction: Choose examples such as a copier, laptop, and ream of paper. Decide which require individual serial tracking and explain the operational reason for each decision.
